atoms.text:
The king stood with his left foot already in the stirrup, his hand in his horse’s mane. He was ready to ride.

He asked Mamad, “Please, would you tell the queen that I will arrive at our home at lunchtime in three days’ time? I would like to have a grand feast when I arrive!”

And with that, the king set off.

atoms.text: After the king had ridden far away, he turned to his guard and laughingly said, “I’ve got him! I am not hunting, and now Mamad will lie to the queen. Mamad will look like such a fool.”

b: He asks Mamad to ride hard and fast to the next village.
++He asks Mamad to tell the queen to have a feast ready in three days time.
++He thinks he has tricked Mamad into lying.
He has played a funny joke on his guard.

atoms.a: Why does the king only tell the guard once they are far away?
b: He forgot to mention it to the guard.

atoms.text:
But, Mamad had earned his reputation. The queen asked Mamad what her king had asked for.

He answered, “Maybe you should prepare a big feast three days from now, maybe not. Maybe the king will be there, maybe not. Maybe he is hunting, maybe not.”
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody rate = '90%'>But, Mamad had earned his reputation. The queen asked Mamad what her king had asked for. He answered, <voice voice='m3'>“Maybe you should prepare a big feast three days from now, maybe not. Maybe the king will be there, maybe not. Maybe he is hunting, maybe not.”</voice></prosody>

atoms.text:
“Well, will the king come or not?” asked the queen, very confused.

Mamad answered, “I am not sure whether the king put his right foot in the stirrup after I left. I am not sure of anything the king did after I saw him.”

I am not sure of anything the king did after I saw him.”</voice></prosody>

atoms.text:
After three days, the king returned joyfully. “Mamad has lied!” he cried to the queen. “I have not been hunting these three days!”

“Mamad has not lied,” answered the queen. “Mamad has only told me what he has seen with his own eyes and nothing more.”

atoms.a: Was the king able to trick Mamad?
Why do you think Mamad kept repeating 'maybe'?
b: ++He did not want to accuse the king of lying.
He was scared of the queen.

atoms.a: Why was the king joyful when he returned?
b: He was looking forward to his feast.
++He thought Mamad fell for his trick.

atoms.a: What do you think the lesson or moral of this story is?
